provenance.l: MER EDL reconstruction (NASA) — Spirit entry 5,630 m/s inertial at −11.5°, 840 kg design mass, β 89.8 kg/m²; chute 251 s at 7.54 km, RAD firing 339.4 s at 99 m, ~14 m/s airbag impact (pre-entry Monte Carlo landing 352 s); bridle cut 8.5 m (reconstructed, preliminary)

Spirit's landing reconstruction (Spaceflight Now, from the JPL briefing, 13 Jan 2004) — bridle cut 28 ft (8.5 m) above the surface; 28 bounces across nearly 1,000 ft, at rest 57 s later; 250–300 m from first impact (Spaceflight Now, 4 Jan 2004). The first bounce height (8.4 m) is from an unopened JPL snippet: drawn as an estimate

MER landing press kit (Jan 2004) — heat shield 20 s after the chute; 20 m bridle spooled out 10 s after it; radar lock about 2.4 km; airbags at 284 m, 8 s before impact (Spirit plan); airbag retraction from 12 min after landing for about an hour, petals open from L+96 min (plan figure, Spirit)
